newsitem.title: UK: RTZ sees sparkling future for India diamonds.
newsitem.headline: RTZ sees sparkling future for India diamonds.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc's Argyle Diamonds said on Wednesday it saw strong growth in India's diamond and diamond jewellery exports continuing, particularly in the U.S. market.

Argyle managing director Gordon Gilchrist told a news conference in Bombay, details of which were published in London, that Argyle, Ashton and RTZ/CRA intended to be long term players in the diamond industry.

RTZ/CRA has a 60 percent stake in Argyle, while Ashton has the remaining 40 percent. The Argyle mine in north western Australia is a leading producer of industrial and gem diamonds. In 1995 diamonds accounted for two percent of RTZ's group sales.
Mike Mitchell, general manager of Argyle's rough diamond sales division, told the news conference, "Strong growth in India's diamond and diamond jewellery exports can be expected to continue."
The group also released the latest results of the Indo-Argyle Diamond Council programmes, which aims to help the Indian industry win market share and reach new customers.

Argyle Diamonds customer service manager Andrew Wagstaff said in the three years since the programme started the overall approval rating for Indian suppliers to the U.S. had risen to more than 55 percent from about 15 percent.

Gilchrist and John Robinson, managing director of Ashton Mining, are due to open a new factory in the SEEPZ trade export zone on Thursday for the InterJewel company, which belongs to the Indo-Argyle Diamond Council. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
